transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function whose body preserves the Rust 1.96 target body as the single delegation `is_ascii(self)`, adapted only by naming the receiver parameter `slice` and disambiguating the private helper as `private_is_ascii(slice)` in the harness namespace.
Adapted the Rust `pub const fn` wrapper to a non-const Verus harness function; no executable control-flow or data-flow step was changed.
Instantiated the generated shared ASCII vocabulary with the frozen definitions of `ascii_is_byte` and `ascii_all`; added `#![auto]` only as a Verus quantifier-trigger annotation.

Declared the private `is_ascii` callee as a narrowly named source-backed boundary for the active x86_64+sse2 Rust helper body. This boundary covers the helper's `const_eval_select` runtime branch, small-slice word loop, remainder iterator check, and SSE2 helper dispatch; the public target wrapper body itself is not external.

Specialized the private-helper boundary to the active verification target after `rustc --print cfg` reported `target_arch="x86_64"` and `target_feature="sse2"`; cfg-excluded non-SSE2 and loongarch helper bodies remain source-indexed but are not claimed in this harness.
